subject: QBR prep: capacity and unit economics — GPU spend, utilization, batching/caching impacts

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: capacity and unit economics — GPU spend, utilization, batching/caching impacts

Team —

As we pull the QBR slides together I want to lock the narrative on two interlocking things: (1) what committed capacity we need for the next 12 months (by pool), and (2) the unit-economics impact of our proposed choices (GPU $/hour, effective tokens/$ after batching + KV caching, and tail-latency tradeoffs). The board will ask for numbers and a short sensitivity analysis.

I attached a working model (qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx) and two exports I pulled from the serving runtime: gpu_util_by_pool.csv and a short batch/latency simulation (batch_latency_sim.pdf). 

Please reply in-thread with the following by EOD today (Sep 28):
- Marcus: updated utilization assumptions per pool and a short note on what we can safely assume for prefix/KV cache hit rate in a conservative vs. aggressive scenario (2 bullets each). If you can include a 3-line recommended autoscale target (min/target/max) per pool that'd be ideal.
- Laura: commercial ask — what committed spend (monthly) would procurement need to start contracting with Nimbus for preferred pricing? Also flag any lead time / SLA-related procurement blockers.
- Hannah: ops/infra knobs — where can we push to reduce unit cost without hurting p99 latency (quantization choices, batch timeout defaults, preferred batch sizes)? Give a recommended delta vs. current defaults.

I'll synthesize replies into a 2-slide packet (capacity assumptions + unit economics sensitivity) for the executive QBR. If anyone needs more telemetry I can ask Data to kick off a quick query but prefer to use the attached exports unless you tell me otherwise.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity and unit economics — GPU spend, utilization, batching/caching impacts

Eve —

Quick pass on the asks below. I validated the numbers in gpu_util_by_pool.csv and ran a conservative + aggressive kernel of the attached spreadsheet. Key takeaways:

1) Baseline utilization (current 30-day avg):
- general-purpose pool (g4/g5-like): 52% avg util, p95 latency cushion ~ 28% headroom before p99 degrades
- high-throughput pool (dense models + batching): 68% avg util, but sensitive to tail requests when batch windows open
- low-latency pool (pinning for interactive chat): 34% avg util, needs headroom for spikes

2) Cache hit assumptions (prefix + KV cache):
- Conservative: 18% effective token hit rate (assumes cold-starts on new prompts, modest reuse)
- Aggressive: 35% effective token hit rate (after routing + prompt-sanitization improvements)

3) Autoscale recommendation (min/target/max nodes):
- gp-pool: 4 / 10 / 18
- ht-pool: 6 / 16 / 28
- ll-pool: 2 / 6 / 12
(These map to expected per-pool QPS under 95th percentile traffic forecasts; margins tuned to preserve p99 under 99th traffic)

4) Unit economics impact: with current spot-like pricing we estimate raw GPU cost per 1M tokens (generation + context) ~ $145 (no caching). Applying conservative cache (18%) drops to ~$119/1M tokens. Aggressive cache (35%) drops to ~$95/1M tokens. Adding batching improvements (reduce avg tokens spent per request by ~6% due to better prefix coalescing) yields additional ~5-7% cost drop.

5) Risk notes: if we push target util > 75% for ht-pool we start to see p99 cliffing for model variants with >1024 context unless we lower batch timeouts; that will increase tail latency by ~80-150ms in our sim. See batch_latency_sim.pdf for the sim runs.

Attached: refined csv (gpu_util_by_pool.csv) and a one-sheet export from the capacity model. Happy to drop a short table into the slide deck.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Marcus —

From procurement's seat: to get a materially better blended rate from Nimbus we need to commit to a minimum monthly $ figure and a 12-month term. Ballpark thresholds we should consider putting on the slide:
- Preferred pricing band A (30% off list): requires ~$1.2M/mo committed spend (12mo)
- Band B (20% off): requires ~$650k/mo committed spend
- Band C (10% off): requires ~$300k/mo committed spend

Lead time / blockers:
- Legal will want the standard infra SLA review and an audit clause for SOC2+; that is ~3 weeks once we hand over the draft contract.
- Nimbus requires a projected utilization profile by pool to validate our sizing request (they'll ask for the util numbers Marcus provided).

Ask for slides: please add a small sensitivity column that shows the blended token $/1M for each commitment band (Marcus' cost numbers + expected list discounts). I can turn that into a procurement recommendation: commit to Band B if the aggressive caching scenario (>=30% hit) is plausible; otherwise stick to Band C for Q1 and reevaluate.

CC'ing Nimbus to open the conversation — Sara, can you confirm lead time for onboarding at these commitment tiers and whether they have any minimum node counts per pool?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is exactly what I needed. Short synthesis for the QBR narrative and owners: 

Slide 1 (Capacity asks & risk): Marcus will own the slide. We will present the 3-pool autoscale targets and show the conservative vs. aggressive cache hit assumptions. Callout: recommend we present the conservative case as the base and the aggressive case as upside.

Slide 2 (Unit economics & procurement): Laura will own the commercial slide. Please include the three Nimbus bands and a blended $/1M token sensitivity column (Marcus to provide the per-token deltas). Recommendation: propose Band B as the board ask if Marcus' aggressive cache >=30% is achievable within Q1 optimizations; otherwise recommend Band C for a conservative approach.

Operational asks (Hannah): please produce a 2-line checklist of infra changes we will commit to for the next quarter (batch timeout change, quantization pilot for non-chat models) and estimate the expected unit-cost delta (e.g., -6% on tokens).

Action items & next steps:
- Marcus: drop the per-pool autoscale numbers into the model and paste the final table in the drive link by EOD Wed (2026-09-30).
- Laura: draft a procurement ask slide with Band C/B pricing bands + recommended ask; include Nimbus lead-time note. Due EOD Wed.
- Hannah: 2-line infra checklist + expected delta. Due EOD Wed.

I'll assemble into a 2-slide PDF for exec review on Thu morning. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Evelyn
